description: A screen identity row and a device row, each carrying the full resource-row baseline and a scope_node placement, are accepted — and both are placed under nodes that are NOT screen-kind (the screen under a group, the device under the site), which is the placement freedom DAT-004 grants. This case no longer claims DAT-004a, despite its frozen case id: the remaining expectations here (that each row's id is the id a screen_id/device_id names, that neither equals any scope-node id in this fixture, that neither placement is the screen-kind node) are properties of the FIXTURE's own chosen constants, true whatever an implementation does, so they cannot detect DAT-004a in either direction. They are kept because they keep this case's DAT-004 claim honest — a fixture that placed a row at the screen-kind node, or reused a node id as a row id, would stop demonstrating placement freedom — not because they test anything. DAT-004a's actual obligation is a REFUSAL (SCREEN_ID_UNRESOLVED) for a screen_id that resolves to a scope node, which no case can observe from a row bundle: it needs a surface that resolves a reference, and the resolution question is settled before any refusal is reached — see conformance/unimplemented-error-codes.json's data-model-1 entry for what every such surface actually does today.
